keyVerseText: And he brought him to Jesus. And when Jesus beheld him, he said, Thou art Simon the son of Jona: thou shalt be called Cephas, which is by interpretation, A stone.
rootMeaning: The word Κηφᾶς (Kēphâs) originates from the Aramaic כֵּיפָא (kêph), meaning 'rock' or 'hollow of a rock.' This Chaldee root conveys the image of a solid, foundational stone, emphasizing stability and strength. Unlike the simple English term 'rock,' the original root evokes both the physicality and protective shelter of a rock's hollow, suggesting a place of refuge and steadfastness.
usageInScripture: Κηφᾶς appears six times in the New Testament, predominantly translated as 'Cephas,' a surname given to Peter. Four occurrences use 'Cephas' directly, while two use 'of Cephas,' indicating possession or association. This consistent translation underscores the personal and foundational identity attributed to Peter in the early Christian community, linking him to the symbolic meaning of a rock.
theologicalSignificance: The name Κηφᾶς carries profound theological weight as it identifies Peter as 'the Rock,' a foundational figure in the establishment of the Church. Understanding its root meaning enriches the recognition of Peter's role not merely as an individual but as a symbol of strength and stability in the faith. This emphasizes Christ's intentional naming, highlighting the divine purpose in Peter's leadership and the Church's enduring foundation. It reminds believers that their faith rests on the unshakable rock of Christ and His appointed witnesses.
keyVerseReflection: In John 1:42, Jesus renames Simon as Cephas, explicitly interpreting it as 'a stone.' This declaration reveals the significance of the name, marking a transformation in Simon's identity and mission. The word Κηφᾶς here conveys more than a label; it signifies the solid foundation upon which Jesus will build His Church, affirming Peter's pivotal role in God's redemptive plan.
